title: Quantum Chemistry & Molecular Orbital Theory
subject: Chemical Physics
summary: Fifty-one short lessons that turn the chemist's orbital pictures into physics: the molecular Hamiltonian and Born-Oppenheimer surfaces, the variational method as the generalized matrix eigenproblem Hc = ScE, group theory built from the great orthogonality theorem, H2+ and H2 from first principles (LCAO, MO versus valence bond), Huckel theory as tight-binding, SALC orbitals of H2O, NH3 and benzene, Walsh diagrams, frontier orbitals and Woodward-Hoffmann as symmetry conservation, then Slater determinants, Hartree-Fock (Fock operator, Roothaan-Hall, SCF, Koopmans), basis sets, electron correlation (CI, size-consistency, MP2, coupled cluster), density functional theory, and a final unit on what computed orbitals and energies mean with a PySCF/Psi4-style workflow. Concept and chemical interpretation first; calculation is a minority of the work.

units.title: The Many-Electron Problem
units.summary: Write down the molecular Hamiltonian in atomic units, separate nuclei from electrons with Born-Oppenheimer to get the potential energy surface chemists draw as reaction coordinates, and meet helium as the smallest system where electron-electron repulsion already forces approximation.

Explain which term makes the problem unsolvable beyond one electron and why the chemist's 'electrons in orbitals' picture is an approximation to it.

lessons.title: From Wavefunctions to Density: the Hohenberg-Kohn Theorems
objectives: Explain why the electron density $\rho(\mathbf r)$ (3 variables) could replace $\Psi$ ($3N$ variables): it fixes $N$ by integration and the nuclear charges and positions through the Kato cusp condition.

State and prove the first Hohenberg-Kohn theorem (reductio ad absurdum with the variational principle) and the second (a variational principle for $E_v[\rho]$ with universal $F[\rho]=T[\rho]+V_{ee}[\rho]$).
Explain that HK is an existence theorem, not a recipe, and why the Thomas-Fermi functional fails.
keyEquations: E_v[\rho]=F[\rho]+\int v(\mathbf r)\rho(\mathbf r)\,d\mathbf r,\qquad F[\rho]=T[\rho]+V_{ee}[\rho]

lessons.title: Kohn-Sham: Non-Interacting Electrons with the Same Density
objectives: Derive the Kohn-Sham construction: $E[\rho]=T_s+\int v\rho+J+E_{xc}$ and the equations $[-\tfrac12\nabla^2+v_{eff}]\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i\varphi_i$ with $\rho=\sum|\varphi_i|^2$ and $v_{xc}=\delta E_{xc}/\delta\rho$.
Define $E_{xc}$ as the sum of exchange, correlation and the kinetic correction $T-T_s$, and compare KS with Hartree-Fock (local $v_{xc}$ with correlation versus non-local exchange without).
State the meaning of KS orbitals (auxiliary; the highest eigenvalue equals $-$IP for the exact functional) and the self-interaction requirement $E_{xc}[\text{one electron}]=-J$.
keyEquations: \left[-\tfrac12\nabla^2+v_{\rm eff}(\mathbf r)\right]\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i\varphi_i,\quad v_{\rm eff}=v+\int\frac{\rho(\mathbf r')}{|\mathbf r-\mathbf r'|}d\mathbf r'+v_{xc}

lessons.title: The Exchange-Correlation Functional Zoo: LDA, GGA and Hybrids
objectives: Describe Jacob's ladder: LDA (uniform gas, $\varepsilon_x\propto\rho^{1/3}$), GGA (PBE, BLYP; $\nabla\rho$), meta-GGA (kinetic energy density), hybrids (B3LYP, PBE0; exact exchange), and double hybrids.
Explain the adiabatic-connection argument for mixing about 25% exact exchange, $E_{xc}=\int_0^1W_\lambda\,d\lambda$, and write $E_{xc}^{\rm PBE0}=0.25E_x^{HF}+0.75E_x^{PBE}+E_c^{PBE}$.
Summarize typical performance: LDA overbinds, GGA reduces the error, hybrids improve barriers and thermochemistry, all at rising cost.

lessons.title: Where DFT Fails: Self-Interaction, Delocalization and Dispersion
objectives: Define self-interaction error ($J$ not exactly cancelled for one-electron densities) and delocalization error (convex $E(N)$ instead of piecewise linear), and give their symptoms: low barriers, stretched H$_2^+$ and charge-transfer errors.
Explain why semilocal functionals miss dispersion, $E_{\rm disp}\approx-C_6/R^6$, and how D3/D4 and non-local functionals repair it; estimate Ar$_2$.
Link to the exact-functional conditions (Koopmans-like HOMO eigenvalue equal to $-$IP, derivative discontinuity) and to remedies (range-separated hybrids).
keyEquations: E_{\rm disp}\approx-\frac{C_6}{R^6}\ \ (\text{damped at short range in D3})

lessons.title: What a Computed Orbital or Energy Actually Means
objectives: Distinguish observables (electron density, energy differences, dipole moment) from model constructs (canonical orbitals, orbital energies, Mulliken charges), and explain the non-uniqueness of occupied orbitals under unitary rotation.

Convert electronic energies into chemically meaningful quantities ($\Delta E_{el}\to\Delta H,\Delta G$ with ZPE and thermal corrections) and relate accuracy to equilibrium constants ($1.364$ kcal/mol per factor of 10).
Interpret common outputs critically: HOMO/LUMO as reactivity descriptors, natural orbital occupations as a multireference diagnostic, population analyses, spin contamination.
keyEquations: \Delta H\approx\Delta E_{el}+\Delta E_{ZPE}+\Delta E_{\rm thermal}+\Delta(pV),\qquad \Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S

lessons.title: Doing It: A PySCF/Psi4-Style Workflow
objectives: Lay out a calculation as a sequence: geometry and charge/multiplicity, method and basis choice, SCF (with convergence checks), geometry optimization on the PES, frequency analysis (minimum versus saddle) and thermochemistry.
Estimate cost and memory from the scaling laws (HF $M^{3-4}$, MP2 $M^5$, CCSD $M^6$, CCSD(T) $M^7$; ERIs $M^4/8$) and choose a method for a given problem.
Design a verification checklist: convergence to the intended state, $\langle S^2\rangle$, imaginary frequencies, basis-set sensitivity, method hierarchy, comparison with experiment.
keyEquations: t_{\rm HF}\sim M^{3\text{-}4},\ t_{\rm MP2}\sim M^5,\ t_{\rm CCSD}\sim M^6,\ t_{\rm CCSD(T)}\sim M^7
